description: La Peace Legit team is filled with PKBM Praxis High School Students, especially level 10. We are seeking experience and hoping that our research could contribute to the world of Science and space exploration.
summary:
Testing rovers and habitat hardware directly on the Moon or Mars is extremely costly and high-risk. Currently, selecting terrestrial analog sites relies heavily on subjective visual comparisons, overlooking critical discrepancies in slope, thermal extremes, and mineral composition.

To address this challenge, we developed A-Pola-GIS (Analog Planetary Orbital & Landscape Geographic Information System). It is an interactive web platform that quantitatively matches Earth landscapes with off-world exploration targets. By integrating open-access multi-mission datasets from NASA and JAXA, our system evaluates site similarity based on four key parameters: surface geology, thermal profiles, slope, and elevation. Users can dynamically adjust parameter weights using mission presets (Landing Safety, ISRU, Habitat Suitability) to instantly generate a data-driven similarity score (0–100%).

A-Pola-GIS is important because it replaces subjective estimation with mathematical precision. It empowers researchers to identify cost-effective, safe analog testbeds on Earth before launch, while providing students and the public with an accessible window into comparative planetary science.
details:
What it does

Imagine being able to "roam" across Earth to find locations with natural conditions most similar to those on the Moon or Mars. That is what A-Pola-GIS does. It is an interactive web platform that allows users to explore 3D maps, spanning Earth’s seven continents, as well as the surfaces of the Moon and Mars. Users can go beyond simple exploration, they can directly and quantitatively compare conditions at a specific location on Earth with those at potential space landing sites.

How it works

Behind the scenes, A-Pola-GIS aggregates and integrates various data, including satellite imagery, topography, temperature profiles, and mineral composition from NASA and other space agency partners. Our system evaluates the similarity between locations based on four key parameters: geology/mineralogy, thermal profiles (temperature), slope, and elevation.

Development Tools & Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure: In developing A-Pola-GIS, our team combined official space agency data repositories with cloud computing and assistive AI tools:

  • Google Colab (Python Environment): Used to write and execute geospatial processing scripts to extract, inspect, and break down raw NASA .tiff (GeoTIFF) raster datasets into structured environmental parameters.
  • Google Gemini: Used to brainstorm project concepts, break down NASA Space Apps Challenge requirements, structure the presentation flow, code for the website, and refine interface/submission copywriting.
  • DeepSeek: Used to assist with writing and debugging Python code for parsing and processing NASA .tiff geospatial raster files in Google Colab.
  • NoteGPT: Used to summarize challenge briefing videos to accelerate initial research and requirement review.
  • ChatGPT: Used to assist the programmer to code the website.
  • Google Ai: Used to assist programmers to code the website.

All planetary and terrestrial datasets, coordinates, and physical metrics were sourced directly from official NASA (Moon Trek, PDS, Earthdata) and JAXA (SELENE/Kaguya) repositories without AI data fabrication.
